URL: https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-july-and-30-september-2026
Also: https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/press-release/energy-price-cap-will-rise-13-july
(Search snippet content)

From 1 July 2026 the Ofgem energy price cap rose by 13%, from £1,641 to £1,862 a year for households paying by Direct Debit with typical usage.

- After updating figures to reflect that households are using less energy than before — around 7% less electricity and 17% less gas compared with the last review — the price cap level from 1 July is £1,663 per year.
- Electricity prices rise by around 5%; gas bills rise by around 24%.
- The increase is driven by higher wholesale gas prices, caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Prices remain below the height of the 2022 energy crisis.
- Around two million people are already in debt to their energy supplier. Average energy debt has risen from £1,848 in 2023-24 to £2,270 in 2025-26.
